title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East (Late Show) on 1970-01-02
lineage: SBD > MR > DAT (x) > CDR (x) > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Superb soundboard capture of a legendary early‑1970 Dark Star with stellar St Stephen, The Eleven and Lovelight.
ai_review.review: The partial recording delivers an outstanding soundboard mix – crystal‑clear drums, forward cymbals and a punchy organ that lets the band’s improvisation shine. Musically it shines on a monster Dark Star that builds into spacey, melodic peaks, followed by a fiery St Stephen, a rousing The Eleven and a raging Lovelight. Although the set is truncated, the performance is consistently praised as one of the best from this era.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews give 5‑star ratings and extol both the musical performance (especially Dark Star) and the superb soundboard quality; only a few note incompleteness, keeping the overall rating just shy of perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, balanced mix with cymbals and snare up front; occasional tape hiss and a small cut in St. Stephen but overall superb clarity and depth.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Partial late‑show segment that flows tightly through a soaring Dark Star into an energetic St. Stephen, then a powerful The Eleven and a rapturous Lovelight; pacing is high‑energy despite the truncation.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for his melodic, soaring guitar work in the later minutes of Dark Star – called one of his best performances.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ on Lovelight is highlighted as a standout; several reviewers speculate about Tom Constanten’s presence on Dark Star.
band_member_comments.Drums: Both Bill Kreutzmann and Mickey Hart are noted for forward‑placed snare, cymbals and overall punchy percussion.
